device: Android phone (user's phone), Qualcomm Adreno-6xx class GPU
canonical_run: mobile-ua (Desktop Site disabled, real Android UA; 2026-10-26)

mobile-ua.mode: Desktop Site disabled (real mobile UA: Linux; Android 10; ... Chrome Mobile)

desktop-site.mode: Desktop Site active (desktop Linux UA; superseded by mobile-ua)

observation.raw: WebGPU output had transparent background but left opaque rails on the image's main object; WASM output was a perfect transparent-background image. Retest with Desktop Site disabled produced 'same result image quality' (opaque rails again).
observation.interpretation: WebGPU (adreno f16=yes) produced a visually defective mask (missing foreground -> opaque rails left on the subject) in both desktop-site and real-mobile-UA modes; WASM produced a clean mask both times. On this Adreno device WebGPU is neither faster (mobile-ua: 6709 ms vs 6600 ms; desktop-site: 6525 ms vs 6457 ms) nor visually reliable, so WASM is the safe default; WebGPU stays an opt-in path.
